scrape.campaign: Custom ERP for small and mid-size manufacturers (Gujarat)
scrape.need: Small and mid-size manufacturers run orders, stock, production and dispatch on Excel and phone calls, with errors and delays, and are growing out of it

need_analysis.summary: Owner-run manufacturing units with roughly 20 to 200 staff in Gujarat run orders, stock, production and dispatch on Excel, Tally and phone calls. Errors and delays hurt more as they grow. The need is structural, so old proof of fit is fine, but a dated trace of growth or of an ops hire is what separates a unit that is ready to buy from one that is merely a manufacturer.
need_analysis.who_has_this_need: Owner-, family- or partner-run manufacturers with many SKUs or make-to-order work, in these clusters: Morbi (ceramics, sanitaryware), Rajkot (engineering, castings, pumps, welding, machined parts), Ahmedabad GIDC (Naroda, Vatva, Odhav, Sanand: plastics, chemicals, packaging, auto parts, cables), Vadodara (fabrication, electrical, machinery) and Surat (textile processing, embroidery, packaging). Units that are about to add a plant, machines or a second shift feel it first.
observable_signals: Raising money or filing for a public issue to fund a new plant or machines (DRHP or IPO of an SME with a prospectus that states staff count, capex and company-published contacts). Tested 26 Oct 2026: Carver Roboweld, Rajkot, 68 permanent + 75 contract staff, DRHP 25 Aug 2026, IPO 28-30 Oct 2026, proceeds for welding robots.
A rating agency note (CARE, ICRA, CRISIL, Acuite, Infomerics) that states a dated capex or new-unit plan for a manufacturer in the target cities

Hiring for ERP executive, MIS executive, production planning (PPC), store/inventory or dispatch roles, where the job text says 'implement ERP', 'Excel MIS', 'Tally' or 'coordinate production with sales' and does not name SAP, Oracle or Dynamics (still on spreadsheets)
Many hires at once or a second unit (growth marker, from a job post or the company's site)
Employee-review text (AmbitionBox, bundled in the Naukri output) saying 'manual work' or 'no system' (supporting hint only)
Size and fit markers on B2B marketplaces (employee band, turnover, GST). These show fit only, not need.
where_signals_show: Exchange and aggregator pages for SME IPO / DRHP filings by city (ipoplatform.com city pages, chittorgarh.com IPO pages, exchange-hosted DRHP PDFs)
Rating agency press releases and rationales (careratings.com, icra.in, crisilratings.com, acuite.in, infomerics.com)
Naukri.com and Indeed India job posts (company-posted, last 14-30 days)
The company's own website: careers, about, plant addresses, contact page
disqualifiers: Already runs SAP, Oracle, Dynamics, Odoo, Zoho or another named ERP (the earlier run dropped Synchro Electricals for Odoo and Filter Concept for 'orders checked in ERP software')
Traders, dealers, wholesalers or shops that do not manufacture
ERP vendors, implementation consultants, staffing firms and software agencies (competitors); e.g. Infinity Infoway and Emipro showed up in a Rajkot 'ERP implementation' job search
Very large listed companies or units of a big group with group IT (Kajaria, Simpolo, RAK Ceramics, Rajoo-class firms)
Fewer than about 20 or more than about 250 people (Antala Industries, Rajkot, has 11 staff and was incorporated Aug 2024, so it is out)
Outside Rajkot, Morbi, Ahmedabad (Naroda, Vatva, Odhav, Sanand), Vadodara, Surat (Mehsana and Gandhinagar are out of scope)
Evidence older than 90 days (before 2026-07-28), except a DRHP still pending approval, which may be kept up to 180 days if flagged
No contact that the business itself published
need_analysis.decision_maker: Owner, managing director or a partner. In larger family units the operations head, works manager or GM. For SME-IPO firms, the promoter or managing director; the company secretary email in the prospectus is only a route in. The HR person who posts a job is not the buyer.

considered.source: SME IPO / DRHP register by city (ipoplatform.com city pages + chittorgarh.com IPO pages + exchange DRHP PDFs)
considered.signal_for_this_need: Strong. A dated public filing from a manufacturer that is raising money for a plant, machines or working capital: a growth moment, with a stated headcount and a promoter who has just promised investors better MIS. Not a proof of pain, but a trigger.
considered.volume_in_geo: Tested 26 Oct 2026: 2026-dated DRHP or IPO events for about 12-14 manufacturers: Ahmedabad (Raj Polypack 30 Sep, Faith Industries 4 Aug, Johnsoncab Electricals 7 Jul, Kumar Cotton Mills 30 Jun, Bipin Offset 4 May, JEE Pumps 19 Apr, Anil Fashions, Parswam Fashion), Rajkot (Weldor CNC Machines 30 Sep, Carver Roboweld IPO 28-30 Oct, Antala Industries, plus two jewellery makers and Vishwas Refoils), Surat (S.R.G. Narrow Fab 30 Sep). Vadodara has none in 2026; the Morbi page is empty.
considered.reachability: Good. The prospectus page publishes company phone, email and website (checked for Carver, Antala, Wiscon, Anand Seamless: all four showed them).
considered.risk: Low. Public pages, no login. Aggregator pages can lag the exchange; the city tables render empty, so only the DRHP cards work. IPO firms may already have an ERP or a finance team; the prospectus must be checked for it.
considered.why: It is the only free source I found that gives a dated event, a stated headcount and a company-published contact in one place, and it shows growth rather than just 'a manufacturer'.

chosen.name: SME IPO / DRHP pipeline of manufacturers in the target cities
chosen.channel_type: statutory filings via free aggregator pages (web)
chosen.how_to_run: 1) WebFetch the four city pages, each of which holds a 'DRHP Filed SME IPOs' card list with company, sector, DRHP date and exchange (the city table itself renders empty, so ignore it): https://www.ipoplatform.com/ipo-insights/geography-wise-ipos/Ahmedabad , /Rajkot , /Surat , /Vadodara . Also WebFetch https://www.ipoplatform.com/ipo/drhp-filed-sme-ipos twice (offset 0 and offset 100000) and keep cards whose city is Ahmedabad, Sanand, Rajkot, Morbi, Surat or Vadodara, and WebFetch https://www.ipoplatform.com/ipo/sme for issues open now. The Morbi page is empty, so for Morbi run one WebSearch: 'Morbi SME IPO DRHP' with allowed_domains chittorgarh.com, ipocentral.in, ipoplatform.com. 2) Keep manufacturing sectors (plastic, chemical, cables, engineering, packaging, textiles, steel, auto, ceramic, pumps, electrical) with an event date (DRHP filed or IPO open/close) on or after 2026-07-28. Keep a DRHP filed earlier in 2026 (for example Johnsoncab 7 Jul, Kumar Cotton 30 Jun, Bipin Offset 4 May, JEE Pumps 19 Apr) only if no IPO has opened, and mark it 'older than 90 days, pending'. 3) For each name open https://www.chittorgarh.com/ipo/<company-name-hyphenated>-ipo/ (confirmed to load for carver-roboweld, antala-industries, anand-seamless, wiscon-industries, core4-engineers, vans-electroengineerings) or WebSearch '<company> IPO chittorgarh' for the slug. If there is no page yet (DRHP only), open the company's ipoplatform detail link (pattern /ipo/<slug>-ipo/<id>), the 'Read DRHP' PDF and the company's own site (use python -I with fitz if the PDF fetch returns binary). 4) Record the fields below. Cost 0; about 12-18 fetches and 2-3 searches in all.
chosen.qualifying_signal: A manufacturer with its plant or registered office in the target cities, with a dated DRHP or IPO event within 90 days (or a pending DRHP up to 180 days, flagged), a stated headcount of about 20-250 (permanent plus contract), objects of issue that include a plant, machines, capacity or working capital, and a phone, email or website published by the company. Reject if the prospectus or site names an in-house ERP such as SAP or Oracle, or if the firm is a trader (Wiscon-type) or has under 20 staff (Antala).
chosen.fields_to_capture: company name; registered office and plant address and city; sector and products; employees (permanent, contract, as-of date); objects of issue and amounts; DRHP date; IPO open, close and listing dates; promoter or MD name as printed; company-published phone, email, website, each with the URL where seen; any mention of ERP, SAP, Tally or Excel in the DRHP; the URL of the page or PDF that gave each fact; signal_date_kind = dated_by_source.
chosen.expected_yield: 5-7 usable candidates. Already confirmed feasible: Carver Roboweld, Rajkot (68 permanent + 75 contract, DRHP 25 Aug 2026, IPO 28-30 Oct 2026). Likely to pass the size check: Weldor CNC Machines (Rajkot), Raj Polypack, Faith Industries, Johnsoncab Electricals, Bipin Offset, JEE Pumps (all Ahmedabad), S.R.G. Narrow Fab (Surat). Expect two or three to drop on size, ERP in use, or a trader profile.

chosen.name: Naukri and Indeed job posts for ERP, MIS and production-planning roles at manufacturers
chosen.how_to_run: Why Apify here: Naukri returns 403 to a plain fetch (tested), and no free source gives dated ops-hiring text. Run A, Naukri, actor valig/naukri-jobs-scraper (id U5tcRMY1heBYd1FYF, $0.00036 per result + $0.0009 per start; fetch-actor-details with output inputSchema only). 15 runs = 3 keyword strings x 5 locations. Input per run: {"keywords":"<K>","location":"<CITY>","sort":"f","jobAge":"30","jobPostType":["1"],"wfhType":["0"],"limit":12}. K = "ERP executive", "MIS executive", "production planning". CITY = Rajkot, Morbi, Ahmedabad, Vadodara, Surat. (jobPostType 1 = company jobs only, jobAge 30 = last 30 days, sort f = by date.) For an empty Morbi run use "MIS executive ceramic" and "store executive tiles". Run B, Indeed, actor kaix/indeed-scraper (id BIeK7ZcYUrdxDgOEQ, $0.00005 per job + $0.00001 per start). 15 runs, same K and cities: {"keyword":"<K>","location":"<CITY>, Gujarat","country":"IN","radius":"25","radiusUnit":"km","sort":"date","fromDays":"14","searchMode":"detailed","maxItems":15}. Note the allowed fromDays values are only 1, 3, 7 and 14; do not pass 30. Fallback if kaix fails: unfenced-group/indeed-in-scraper {"query":"<K>","location":"<CITY>, Gujarat","radius":25,"sort":"date","fromDays":"14","maxItems":15}. Run one 3-result trial of each actor first. Cost about $0.078 for Naukri + $0.012 for Indeed = about $0.09; abort any run that goes past $0.01. Post-filter in code: drop consultant and staffing posts; keep the post only if the text shows manufacturing context (manufacturing, production, plant, factory, GIDC, machines) AND an ops-system phrase (implement ERP, ERP coordinator, Tally, Excel, MIS, production plan, BOM, MRP, stock register, dispatch); drop vendors and agencies (ERP software, implementation consultant, 'our clients'); drop posts that name SAP, Oracle, Dynamics, Odoo or Zoho as the system in use. Use Naukri company.websiteUrl and company.address for identity, and the bundled AmbitionBox review text as a hint only.
chosen.qualifying_signal: A company-posted job dated within the last 30 days (Naukri createdDate; Indeed posting date within 14 days) at a manufacturer in the target cities, for an ERP, MIS, PPC, store or dispatch role, whose text points to spreadsheet or Tally work or says 'implement ERP'. Several posts from the same firm in the same fortnight count more than one.
chosen.fields_to_capture: company name; job title; city; vacancies; posting date and the field it came from (signal_date_kind = dated_by_source); job URL; the exact phrase that shows the need; whether the poster is the company or a consultant; company website and address (Naukri); salary band as a size hint; AmbitionBox dislike text if present; whether it also appears on the other board.
chosen.expected_yield: 3-5 usable candidates (the earlier run got 8 signal posts from about 300 results, of which about half were real manufacturers with a findable website). Contacts will mostly need a second lookup on the company's own site.

chosen.name: Rating-agency notes that state a capex or new-unit plan for manufacturers in the target cities
chosen.channel_type: financial disclosures (rating press releases) via web search
chosen.how_to_run: Use WebSearch (mode standard) with allowed_domains [careratings.com, icra.in, crisilratings.com, acuite.in, infomerics.com, brickworkratings.com] and these queries, one per cluster: 1) 'Rajkot manufacturer rating rationale 2026 capex new plant bank facilities'; 2) 'Morbi ceramic OR sanitaryware OR vitrified rating 2026 capex new unit'; 3) 'Ahmedabad Naroda OR Vatva OR Odhav OR Sanand manufacturer rating 2026 capex expansion'; 4) 'Vadodara manufacturer rating 2026 capex'; 5) 'Surat manufacturer rating 2026 capex expansion'. Add the words 'August', 'September' or 'October 2026' if the first pass shows only older notes. The date is in the URL or file name (CARE: yyyymmdd at the start of the PDF name; CRISIL: the month and day in the file name; ICRA: the date in the document). Keep notes dated on or after 2026-07-28. CRISIL notes are HTML and load with WebFetch; CARE and ICRA PDFs come back as binary, so save them and extract text locally with python -I and fitz (works on this machine). Then, for each kept firm, WebSearch '<company> Rajkot OR Morbi OR Ahmedabad official website' to find the contact the business itself published. Cost 0; about 5-8 searches (watch the quota: if it blocks, stop and say so). Test results so far: Essen Speciality Films (CARE, Dec 2025, Rs 50 crore new Lothda plant, done Mar-Apr 2026) is too old and Simpolo, Kajaria and RAK are too big, so expect most hits to be dropped on date or size.
chosen.qualifying_signal: A manufacturer with its plant in the target cities, with a rating note dated within 90 days that states a new unit, capacity addition or capex plan with an amount and a timeline, a size that fits 20-250 staff (check turnover below about Rs 300 crore and headcount on the company's site or listing), not a listed large cap, and no named in-house ERP.
chosen.fields_to_capture: company name; city and plant location; rating agency and note date (signal_date_kind = dated_by_source); URL of the note; the capex or expansion sentence and amount; turnover or capacity figures; any statement about systems or MIS; company website and published contact with URL; why the size fits or not.
chosen.expected_yield: 2-4 usable candidates; contact lookup is a second step and fit is the weak point.

plan_round1.if_low_yield: Do these in order. 1) Cross-match: look for any firm that appears in two of the three sources (for example an IPO or rating-note firm that is also hiring an ops role); that is the strongest lead. 2) Use the job actor as a targeted checker: valig accepts company names in 'keywords', so run each shortlisted IPO or rating firm as a keyword (about $0.002 each) to see whether it is hiring ops roles. 3) Widen the job search: keywords 'dispatch coordinator', 'store officer', 'purchase executive Tally', 'planning executive', 'back office executive' plus industry words (tiles, foundry, pump, plastic), and add Sanand, Naroda, Vatva, Odhav, Shapar and Khirasara as separate location strings; fall back to unfenced-group/indeed-in-scraper. 4) Add a size-qualified fit pool (scrapesage/tradeindia-scraper, 26-250 employees, $0.0017 per record) or sourabhbgp/indiamart-scraper for Morbi and Rajkot, and keep only firms that also match a signal from steps 1-3. 5) Look at recently listed SME companies in the cities (listed in the last 180 days, via chittorgarh.com listing pages) for capex announcements. 6) After the Nov-Dec 2026 trade shows open, pull exhibitor lists (skython/exhibitor-list-scraper, $0.0045 per exhibitor) as a fit pool. 7) Google Maps (compass/crawler-google-places) with a manufacturer category and a website as a last-resort fit pool, then check each website's careers page by hand."

fit.rationale_quality: Good and specific for the job-post and SME-IPO sources, weak for rating notes. The need analysis names the buyer, the clusters, the disqualifiers (already on SAP/Odoo, vendors, traders, size, Gandhinagar and Mehsana out of scope) and the signal types. The 15 rejections give tested, concrete reasons: GIDC draw lists were opened and found to list people with no business contact, Naukri returns 403, no association directories were found, and TradeIndia and IndiaMART showed no need signal. Two weaknesses. (1) The plan chose rating notes while its own tests (Essen too old, Simpolo, Kajaria and RAK too big, notes carry no headcount) already pointed to near-zero yield. The run confirmed it: 15 in-window notes opened, 1 candidate, 0 usable. (2) The SME-IPO choice is clever but biased. It tests growth, not the ERP gap, and it selects firms that have merchant bankers, company secretaries and finance staff, so they are the most likely to already run a system. Only 2 of 8 IPO-source candidates have text from the filing about how they work (SRG: 'IT systems'; Bipin: a 'job monitoring sheet'). Morbi, a named cluster, got nothing from any of the three sources and no replacement source was tried.
suspicious_candidates: Techno Instruments (rank 9): the plant is at Santej, which sits in Gandhinagar district. The plan puts Gandhinagar out of scope and the collector dropped Flextron (Jalundra, Gandhinagar) on that ground. It was kept anyway on a 'Gandhi Road, Ahmedabad' label in the job post. Inconsistent, and it should be dropped unless an Ahmedabad plant is confirmed.

Aditya Creative Ornaments (rank 11): breaks the plan's own disqualifier 'no contact that the business itself published'. The company site returned 403 and the contacts are an aggregator copy. Jewellery ERPs are also common, and the objects of issue already include Rs 0.62 cr for design software.
MTE Structures (rank 14): 209 to 229 staff, above the 200 band, Rs 248 cr revenue, a Savli site outside Vadodara city, and likely group IT. It sits at the edge of the plan's size and geography rules.

Cambay Technopack (rank 10): plant city not verified (the name suggests Khambhat), the Vesu office is the only Surat link, the role is junior, and the text says 'Excel/software', which leaves room for an existing system. Labelled 'Surat' without proof.

Raj Polypack, United Techfab and Anil Fashions (ranks 15 to 17): fit-only padding. Plant location (Raj Polypack) and headcount are unknown or stale (United Techfab's is 2 years old, with Rs 763 cr turnover and mostly trading). The Raj Polypack email is an onmicrosoft alias. Anil Fashions has 41% trading. They do not meet the plan's own qualifying signal, which requires a stated headcount of 20 to 250.

Maxwell Engineering, Solanki Mechanic Works and Carver Roboweld: tier 'verified' (Carver also confidence 'high') although only Chittorgarh summaries were read, not the DRHP or RHP. Their ERP use is unknown. Solanki's contacts are an aggregator copy, its 80+ staff is a site claim, and sales fell 53%. The judge summary itself says only the SRG and Bipin DRHPs were read, so these labels are inflated.

Girnar Machine (rank 6): the headcount may be under 20 (directories say 11 to 50), and the 'MS Office, or ERP or any Billing Software' wording is generic template language, not proof of Excel use. The job page was never opened.
Bipin Offset (rank 2): the DRHP is 175 days old, kept under the 180-day allowance without confirming it is still pending. The flag is disclosed, which is honest, but 'verified' is shaky on timing.

Omval Controls (rank 13): no tool is named in the post and the Excel link is inferred. '5 vacancies' on Naukri is often a multi-opening setting, so it is weak evidence of scaling. It is correctly marked low.
sources_that_should_have_been_considered: Cross-match of the IPO and rating-note shortlist against job posts. This was step 2 of the plan's own if_low_yield list, costs about $0.002 per firm with valig keyword search, and was never run, so every candidate has multi_source false. It would have been the strongest evidence available.

Export-promotion council member and RCMC directories (EEPC India Gujarat members, Plexconcil, CHEMEXCIL, Indian Council of Ceramic Tiles and Sanitaryware). They are public lists of Gujarat manufacturer-exporters, and exporters need per-order documents and tracking. This could also have filled the Morbi gap.

A Morbi-specific source. All three chosen sources returned nothing for Morbi, a named top cluster. Morbi tile and sanitaryware expo exhibitor lists, the Morbi ceramic association and cluster portals, or Gujarati-language business press were not tried.

Gujarati-language news search (Divya Bhaskar, Sandesh, Gujarat Samachar business pages) for plant-expansion and 'new unit' items about 20 to 200 staff units. The plan rejected news only because English-language, US-only WebSearch found large firms.
Vibrant Gujarat regional-summit MoU and investment lists (Rajkot, Vadodara, Surat) and iNDEXTb project lists, which are dated, named capex commitments from mid-size manufacturers.
Company-name keyword check on valig and Indeed for the 8 IPO-source shortlist firms, to see whether each is hiring ops, store, PPC or MIS roles. This was cheap and not run.

Widened job queries from the plan's own fallback list ('dispatch coordinator', 'store officer', 'purchase executive Tally', 'planning executive') and the GIDC locations Sanand, Naroda, Vatva, Odhav, Shapar and Khirasara. Only 'production planning' and PPC queries produced real manufacturers, and the 'ERP' and 'MIS' queries were mostly noise.
fit.notes: Overall, the sources follow from the need better than a stock recipe would. The IPO and DRHP register is a distinctive, tested choice, and it produced the only filing text with a named manual process (Bipin's job sheet) and a stated headcount inside the band (SRG). Job posts are the right place to catch the need in the company's own words. The rating-note source was a poor bet that the plan's own evidence undercut, and the run reports its failure honestly. The weak spots are as follows. (1) Zero Morbi coverage, and nothing replaced it. (2) No cross-matching between sources, so every candidate is single-source. (3) Several rank decisions break the plan's own rules: Techno Instruments (Gandhinagar plant), Aditya (aggregator-only contacts), MTE (over 200 staff) and three fit-only padding entries at ranks 15 to 17. (4) 'Verified' and 'high' labels sit on candidates whose filings were not read. The judge summary's usable_count of 14 is generous. Applying the plan's own disqualifiers strictly gives about 10: SRG, Bipin, Carver, Maxwell, Solanki, Weldor, Girnar, Sarda, Astek (low) and Omval (low). Even so, the minimum of about 8 is plausibly met, and the run reports never overstate: the rating-note failure, the 403 and 401 blocks, the Morbi gap, the dropped candidates and the unknowns are all disclosed. I judged from the evidence supplied and did no web verification.

chosen.name: Google Maps clinics with no website or an unclaimed profile (Mehsana, Gandhinagar, Ahmedabad)
chosen.how_to_run:
Actor: compass/crawler-google-places. Run 3 times, one location each (the actor takes one location per run), same settings: website="withoutWebsite", language="en", countryCode="in", scrapePlaceDetailPage=false, scrapeContacts=false, no other add-ons. Set the run's max total charge to 0.10 USD.
Run A: {"searchStringsArray":["dentist","skin clinic dermatologist","eye clinic","physiotherapy clinic"],"locationQuery":"Mehsana, India","maxCrawledPlacesPerSearch":3,"website":"withoutWebsite","countryCode":"in"} (12 places).
Run B: same, locationQuery "Gandhinagar, India", terms [dentist, skin clinic dermatologist, physiotherapy clinic], maxCrawledPlacesPerSearch 2 (6 places).
Run C: same, locationQuery "Ahmedabad, India", terms [dentist, skin clinic dermatologist, physiotherapy clinic], maxCrawledPlacesPerSearch 2 (6 places).
Price: 24 places x (0.003 + 0.001 website filter) = about 0.096 USD. Do not use the category filter or skipClosedPlaces (each adds 0.001 per place); filter locally instead.
After the run, keep a row only if: categoryName matches dent|skin|derma|eye|ophthal|physio; permanentlyClosed and temporarilyClosed are false; title is not a chain or hospital; address is in one of the 3 cities; website is empty (a Facebook/Instagram/Justdial/Practo link also counts as no own site if one is returned); phone is present. Rank claimThisBusiness=true and low reviewsCount first. Then run one free WebSearch per survivor ("<clinic name> <city>") to confirm there is no own site and that it is not part of a chain. Optional liveness check on the final shortlist from the leftover budget: compass/Google-Maps-Reviews-Scraper with the placeIds, maxReviews=1, reviewsSort="newest" (0.00045 per review) to get the date of the latest patient review.
Backup if compass gives too few: blackfalcondata/google-maps-no-website-leads-scraper with {"searchTerms":["dentist","skin clinic","physiotherapy"],"locations":["Mehsana, Gujarat","Gandhinagar, Gujarat","Ahmedabad, Gujarat"],"gl":"in","requirePhone":true,"maxResults":12,"searchRadiusKm":15} at 0.0026 per place (it also gives a lead score that uses claim status).
chosen.qualifying_signal: A live Google Maps listing for an independent clinic in the three cities whose website field is empty (or only a social/directory link), with claimThisBusiness=true or a thin profile (few reviews, no hours), a business-published phone, and a free web check that finds no own website. The evidence is the listing URL (url / mapsUrl) plus the scrapedAt date. fit.rationale_quality: Specific and mostly well-argued. The plan first lists observable signals of this need: an empty or social-only website field, an unclaimed profile, Meta ads that send people to WhatsApp or a call, and front-desk or marketing hiring. It then picks one source per signal. Maps shows the gap itself, the ad library shows paid intent with a start date, and job posts show enquiries handled by hand. It rejects Justdial, Practo and DocIndia because they list clinics without showing the gap, and the DocIndia rejection rests on a page the planner actually opened. Registers, associations, news and exhibitors are rejected on evidence that they have no need signal or no reachable list. Two weaknesses. Cost and feasibility were not tested before planning: the planned Maps actor needs a 0.50 USD minimum cap, so both Maps-based sources had to switch actors. The plan also relied on claimThisBusiness, which came back null for 23 of 24 rows.
suspicious_candidates: Nilkanth Hi Tech Dental Hospital (Mehsana, rank 12): 'Hospital' in the name, entity_type unclear, 430 reviews. It may be a multi-doctor hospital, which the brief excludes.

Vinayak Dental Clinic and Implant Center (Nikol, rank 21): Maps category is 'Hospital', the ad is 'Managed By @gjs531' so an agency may run it, the ad phone differs from the Maps phone, and its site is a half-built DrXPro template.

Dentistium Multispeciality Dental Clinic (rank 11): employer name 'Dentistium Clinics (R)', five doctors, five openings, CGHS-empanelled. Likely a group or multi-branch operation, and the job posts were not opened.
Ahmedabad Dental (rank 13): generic name, 719 reviews, booking link goes to Justdial. It may be a multi-branch brand and web search found no match.
Avadhoot Ayurveda (rank 25): outside the dentist, skin, eye and physio scope. Ajara Aesthetics (rank 24): may be a beauty parlour with a visiting doctor.
S M Wellness (rank 3): 'Wellness' name with possible other branches, and it was found by scraper only. Dr. Dhamelia's Skin Laser (rank 27): partly a training business, 10 reviews, ads 8 months old.

Pramukh Dental Clinic (rank 4) and Swastik Physiotherapy (rank 9): both have a working Grexa microsite, which sits close to the disqualifier 'already has a working website'. Rank 9 also has no WhatsApp CTA.

Rank 22 VK Physiotherapy and rank 10 Pimple Post: existence rests on the job post alone, with no usable phone (6146092114 is WorkIndia's shared number). Rank 17 Novoris and rank 20 Maitri are in the same position. These are not reachable as they stand.

Ranks 32 to 38 (Om Dental plus the six carried-over Maps rows) and ranks 28 to 31 (chairside-assistant 'fit only' posts): labelled unverified or fit_only, so they should not count as leads. Rank 14 Siddhi's ad started 97 days ago, just past the 90-day rule, though it is still active.

Rank 6 House of Dentistry, rank 11 Dentistium: the phone numbers come from third-party directories and the employer-to-directory match is by name and area only. They are correctly flagged as not clinic-published but should not be treated as confirmed.
fit.notes: Verdict: the sources follow from the need, and the run reports are candid about what failed. The failures reported are the compass actor refused under the 0.10 cap, all 24 Maps rows being dentists, claim status null, Maps and Ad Library pages unopenable, no Mehsana or Gandhinagar ads, 0 Indeed rows, and a shared WorkIndia phone number. The yield claim is honest but generous. usable_count 27 of 38 correctly excludes the 7 unverified and 4 fit_only entries. It still counts as usable several low-confidence, out-of-scope or unclear entries, and four job-post leads with no phone or other way to reach them. A stricter reading still gives well over the target of about 8 reachable, signal-backed leads: Dabhi's, Sure Align, SM Wellness, Pramukh, Uma Dental, Mehsana Dental, Dr Teeth and Siddhi, all with phones. So enough = true holds. The set is skewed to dentists and to Ahmedabad. Skin, eye and physio were never searched on Maps because the first term filled the per-city cap, and Mehsana and Gandhinagar come only from Maps. The headline signal 'unclaimed profile' was not obtained for any candidate. Most 'verified' tiers rest on scraper data plus one opened page, not an opened Maps or ad page. The most useful finding was a dead or placeholder domain in the Maps website field (Dabhi's NXDOMAIN, Sure Align coming-soon). The plan did not target it, and it should become a deliberate source. The need key in the input is 'clinic-web'. I set need_id to 'clinic-website' as the task instructed. I made no web calls; the judgement comes from the evidence supplied.
sources_that_should_have_been_considered: Google Ads Transparency Center: clinics paying for Google Search ads with no site or a dead landing page, the same intent signal as Meta ads but for people who search on Google, which is the need's stated trigger.

A systematic DNS/HTTP liveness check on every Maps website field (dead, parked, coming-soon or expired domains), not only empty fields. Dabhi's and Sure Align were the two strongest finds and came from this kind of check by luck.
Per-specialty Maps runs, one term per run (skin, eye, physio), so the non-dental specialties named in the need are actually covered.

Mining Google Maps review text for 'phone not answering', 'appointment' and 'WhatsApp' complaints. The plan kept this only as a late fallback, although the plan itself lists patient reviews as an observable signal.
Doctor-listing pages that show 'Claim profile' (DocIndia and similar) as a source of unclaimed-profile evidence. One such page proved useful for Maitri Dental, but it was not planned as a source.
WhatsApp Business or wa.me links in Maps and ad data, to separate clinics that already have a WhatsApp number from those that have none.
